title: Hamburg Sustainability Conference (HSC) Youth Ambassador Program 2027
overview: Young sustainability leaders from Global South countries are selected as HSC Youth Ambassadors. They attend an HSC Youth Roundtable Series in December 2026 and the Hamburg Sustainability Conference on 31 May - 1 June 2027. The organiser describes participation as fully funded, with travel and accommodation covered.
city: Hamburg (conference); Roundtable Series location not stated on the 2027 pages read
program_dates: HSC Youth Roundtable Series: December 7-11, 2026. Hamburg Sustainability Conference: May 31 - June 1, 2027.
deadline_text: Application deadline: October 19, 2026 ("Apply by October 19, 2026 to join us for the HSC Youth Roundtable Series in December"). Interviews with short-listed candidates at the end of October 2026; participation confirmed end of October / early November 2026.
funding_details: Application form page: 'Your travel and accommodation costs are covered.'
No application or participation fee is mentioned on the pages read
participation_fee: None mentioned on the official pages read
eligibility: Come from and reside in a Global South country, based on the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients; only countries in the form's dropdown are eligible
A young leader actively driving sustainability efforts in your community
Can communicate confidently in English and dedicate time to the programme
Available to travel for the Roundtables on December 7-11, 2026 and to attend HSC on May 31 - June 1, 2027
Prior participation in international conferences or youth programmes is asked about but 'is not a mandatory requirement'
nationality_requirements: Country of origin and residence must be in the form's dropdown (OECD DAC ODA recipients). 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' appears in the dropdown of the 2027 application form (checked 2026-10-12).
experience_requirement: Active sustainability engagement in your community; previous international conference experience not mandatory
other_requirements: Availability for the December 7-11, 2026 Roundtable Series (travel required) and the May 31 - June 1, 2027 conference
documents_required: Online form only: personal details, country of origin and residence, occupation, themes, LinkedIn profile link

Written answers: your sustainability work so far and plans; which HSC 26 session you would have joined and why; an example of private-sector collaboration with government or civil society in your country; prior international conferences or youth programmes
application_process: Complete the online form at the official site by October 19, 2026
Short-listed candidates are interviewed at the end of October 2026
Participation confirmed end of October / early November 2026

sources.label: HSC Youth Ambassador Program 2027 application form

eligibility_reason: Age, DRC origin and residence (DRC is in the form's country list) and English are met by the recorded profile. The programme requires 'a young leader actively driving sustainability efforts in your community', which the profile does not record.
potential_issues: Deadline is October 19, 2026 with no time zone stated; submit well before
The December 2026 Roundtable location is not named on the 2027 pages read, so a second visa may be needed besides the Schengen visa for Germany
Meals, visa fees and insurance are not mentioned in the coverage wording
Highly competitive: the 2026 cohort had 16 ambassadors
benefits: Funded travel and accommodation for the Roundtable Series and the Hamburg conference
Speaking, moderation and workshop roles with high-level decision-makers at HSC
relevance_reason: Two funded international trips and high-level networking, with no degree condition and the DRC explicitly listed. Fit depends on demonstrable sustainability work, which the profile does not record, and on making the very short deadline.

visa.required: Yes (Schengen visa for Germany; Roundtable host country not stated)

action: Apply on the official form before October 19, 2026 only if you can describe concrete sustainability or community work; keep December 7-11, 2026 free for the Roundtables.
notes: Lead from Opportunity Desk / Opportunities for Africans. Facts read on the organiser's 2027 pages; aggregators' 'program fees covered' wording was not found on the official pages.

title: Graduate Horizons 2027: master's scholarship application mentorship for displaced African learners
overview: A free mentorship programme that helps African learners with a forced displacement background apply for fully funded master's scholarships starting in 2027, focusing on Mastercard Foundation partner universities (Oxford, Cambridge, Sciences Po, UC Berkeley, CMU-Africa, UGHE, UM6P, AIMS, AUC, AUB) and other scholarships with upcoming deadlines.
program_dates: Mentorship during the 2026-27 scholarship application season; information sessions on 8, 15 and 22 October 2026
deadline_text: Application deadline: Sunday, 25th October, 5 pm BST (UK time). Information sessions: October 15th, 1pm BST; October 22nd, 3pm BST.
funding_details: The programme is mentorship and resources for scholarship applications, not a scholarship itself
The targeted scholarships are described as covering 'tuition, visas & travel, and living costs'
No fee for the mentorship is mentioned on the page read
participation_fee: None mentioned on the page read
eligibility: Interest in pursuing a Master's degree in 2027 with a full scholarship
nationality_requirements: African learners with a forced displacement background; no country list stated on the page read
education_requirement: Unknown / Not specified (aimed at people applying for a master's in 2027)
other_requirements: A Gmail/Google login is needed to open the full details and application form
application_process: Optionally join an online information session (15 or 22 October 2026)
Open the full details and Google Form linked from the UNHCR Rwanda notice and apply by 25 October 2026, 5 pm BST

sources.label: UNHCR Rwanda Help: Call for applications to mentorship for master's degree and scholarship application (deadline 25 October 2026)

eligibility_reason: The applicant is African and holds a bachelor's degree, so a 2027 master's is plausible. The deciding criterion is a forced displacement background (refugee, asylum seeker, internally displaced or stateless), which the profile does not record.
potential_issues: Only for learners with a forced displacement background
The RLRH/Oxford Refugee Studies Centre pages and the Google Form could not be read (403 / login required); details come from UNHCR Rwanda's republication of the call
Mentorship only: it does not itself fund study
benefits: Mentorship and resources for applications to Mastercard Foundation partner universities and other funded master's programmes
relevance_reason: Directly supports applications to several master's scholarships already tracked in this database (Mastercard Foundation at Cambridge, Sciences Po, Edinburgh), but it is restricted to people with a forced displacement background.
action: If you have a forced displacement background (including internal displacement), open the call in a browser with a Google account, read the full criteria and apply before 25 October 2026, 5 pm BST.
notes: Lead from Global South Opportunities. RLRH is hosted with the Refugee Studies Centre, University of Oxford; its news page returned a bot challenge. Facts here come from the UNHCR Rwanda Help notice dated 2 October 2026.

title: Objectif 2030: free certified online courses on environment and sustainable development (IFDD / OIF)
organization: Institut de la Francophonie pour le développement durable (IFDD), Organisation internationale de la Francophonie, with Université Senghor
overview: A series of eight free French-language MOOCs (CLOM) on sustainable development, environmental economics, environmental law, environmental assessment, environmental technologies, environmental careers, climate and biodiversity finance, and sustainable agriculture. Each course runs as a dated session and gives a free certificate of completion to those who pass the quizzes.
program_dates: Sessions listed on the MOOC page: Technologies de l'environnement 5 Oct - 29 Nov 2026 (in progress); Économie de l'environnement et gestion des ressources naturelles 30 Nov - 27 Dec 2026; Comprendre et analyser les enjeux et les actions du développement durable 4 - 31 Jan 2027; Introduction à la finance climat et biodiversité 1 Feb - 14 Mar 2027; Droit et protection de l'environnement 15 Mar - 11 Apr 2027; Pratiques d'agriculture durable et opportunités d'emplois pour les jeunes 19 Apr - 23 May 2027; Métiers de l'environnement 24 May - 18 Jul 2027; Évaluation environnementale: no session dates listed.
deadline_text: No registration deadline stated. Each course runs as a session with fixed dates; quizzes close at the end of the session.
funding_details: Official site: 'Toutes nos formations sont gratuites.'
Certificate: 'une attestation de formation totalement gratuite'
participation_fee: None: 'Toutes nos formations sont gratuites' (official site)
eligibility: 'Il n'y a pas de prérequis pour vous inscrire' (Technologies de l'environnement page); the site says the training is 'accessible à tous'
Interest in the environment and an internet connection
language_requirement: Courses and pages are in French
other_requirements: Certificate (Technologies de l'environnement): at least 50% correct answers in at least 3 of the 11 themes
application_process: Create an account on objectif2030.org and register for the chosen course
Complete the modules and quizzes before the session ends to obtain the certificate

sources.label: Les Opportunités: Technologies de l'environnement listing

eligibility_reason: The official pages state there are no prerequisites and that the courses are open to all; the applicant speaks French.
potential_issues: A certificate of completion, not a degree or a funded mobility
The OIF course 'Découvrabilité et politiques culturelles à l'ère du numérique' seen in the same feed is not on this platform and is not covered by this record
benefits: Free certificates in environmental economics, climate finance and sustainable development, useful for policy and programme-coordination CVs
Self-paced within each session, around 2h30 per week according to the site
relevance_reason: Free, open to all and in French, so fully accessible. It adds credentials in sustainability and climate finance that can strengthen applications to policy fellowships, but it offers no travel or funding.
action: Create a free account on objectif2030.org and register for 'Économie de l'environnement et gestion des ressources naturelles' (30 Nov - 27 Dec 2026) or 'Introduction à la finance climat et biodiversité' (from 1 Feb 2027).
notes: Umbrella record for the OIF/IFDD free online trainings seen in Les Opportunités feeds ('Économie de l'environnement', 'Technologies de l'environnement').
